Favier, A., De Wolf, C., Scrivener, K. and Habert, G. (2018). A sustainable future for the European cement and concrete industry: Technology assessment for full decarbonisation of the industry by 2050. ETH Zurich and EPFL, commissioned by the European Climate Foundation. No DOI or report number printed in the held copy (an ETH Research Collection record may exist - look up).

96-page technology assessment of decarbonisation levers for the EU cement and concrete chain. Targeted pass: Sect. 4.1-4.2 (clinker and cement levels), Sect. 5 (alternative binders, CCS), Annex 1 (model inputs). Loaded: kiln thermal energy by kiln class (Annex, reprinted from CSI-GNR) and the BAT 3000 MJ/t; 875 kg CO2-eq/t clinker; CO2 reduction potentials of alternative binders (Sect. 5.1 text and Annex model values, kept as separate contexts); CCS options with absolute investment, cost increase and CO2 per t clinker (reprinted from CSI/ECRA 2017, held as csi-ecra_2017_001); VRM/HPGR investment; new cement plant 150 EUR/t-yr; clinker shares (flows). Not loaded: scenario results (Sect. 6), concrete, structure and recycling levers, policy (Sect. 7): sector-level or qualitative. Absolute investments carry no plant capacity, so they are not put per unit. Locators are printed page numbers, which equal PDF pages. Traps: EU average 3300 MJ/t (p.24) vs 3702.77 MJ/t (Annex p.88); alternative-binder average 495 (p.50) vs 490 (p.90); Annex cites "Habert et al. [57]" but ref 57 is Dewald and Achternbosch 2016; Annex limestone and calcined-clay CO2 denominators ambiguous (kept in other-values); CCS "CO2 saving" read as captured CO2; price year not stated (2018 used).
